chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from a man, from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Darir, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:
When the Caliph arrives in Egypt from the various provinces, he gathers the people with him; this is not for anyone else.

key_terms.لَيْسَ ذَلِكَ لِأَحَدٍ غَيْرِهِ: This is not for anyone else (exclusive right)

ai.seo_question: What is the exclusive right of the Caliph when arriving in Egypt according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the political and religious authority of the Caliph (often interpreted in Shia discourse as the Imam or the divinely appointed leader) to convene public assemblies, a prerogative exclusive to him. It underscores the concept of *wilayah* in governance, where the leader's arrival in a province like Egypt signifies the restoration of order and the right to address the community, distinguishing his status from other officials.
